_comment: Report <-> app section contract. The Markdown report (birding/report.py) is
the source of truth for what each section is called, what order sections
appear in, and which sections carry a rendered map. The app mirrors that
content; only navigation differs (a Contents menu instead of one long page).
Kept as a fixture so BOTH repos can enforce it:
- birding-app/tests/dom.test.js       asserts the app matches this file.
so renaming a report section without updating the app fails CI.
'report' is a PREFIX of the heading report.py emits (several headings have
dynamic tails, e.g. county names or a year); '*' stands for an f-string slot.
'map' is the app's map container id, non-null only where the report embeds
reportSectionsAppOmits is a map of heading prefix -> WHY the app omits it.
It used to be a bare list, which made it an unaudited escape hatch: adding
a heading to it silently dropped that section from the app forever and the
TOC test still went green. Every entry now needs a reason, and PARITY.md
must carry a matching row - both repos assert it.

menu.label: 📆 Due back soon
menu.why: app-only (F11 part 2): the arrival dates come from sweeping GBIF for every species in the region - hundreds of calls, resumable, cached on the device. The report is built once from a fixed snapshot and committed; a section whose whole value is 'what changes between now and three weeks from now' is a live question, and printing a static answer to it in a document dated today would be worse than not printing it. Owner decision 2026-08-12: the app may carry sections the report does not, as long as the delta is written down.

menu.label: 🔎 Stakeout bird
menu.why: app-only: a Markdown report cannot take a query. The nearest report equivalent, All unseen reports, only covers birds you HAVEN'T seen, and the entire point of a lookup is asking about a bird you already have - 'where can I find a Western Kingbird' is a valid question with a complete year list. Printing every species' places for a whole region is not a section, it is a phone book.

menu.label: 🏞 Stake out a hotspot
menu.why: app-only, and for the same reason as Stakeout bird above: a Markdown report cannot take a query. It is the INVERSE of every place-finding section - those answer 'which place should I go to', this one starts from 'I have chosen this place, tell me everything'. It leads with the PATTERN (how often the place is birded, what a visit is usually worth, who the regulars are) rather than with today rows, because eBird embargoes checklists for an hour and people submit hours later - measured 2026-08-22, three target species returned ZERO reports from that day statewide at 10:10.

menu.label: ⭐ Iconic spots near me
menu.why: F156. APP-ONLY, and deliberately so: the numbers come from GBIF's keyless occurrence facets measured against the reader's own home and chase radius, which a Markdown report generated hours earlier cannot ask for. Ranks how much a place stands out for a bird rather than how rare the bird is, so it surfaces birds no rarity feed ever flags.

menu.label: 🏅 Break a record
menu.why: app-only (F137): the model needs GBIF and decades of history, so it is computed OFFLINE and shipped as a bundled asset - scripts/pack_state_records.py, 222 KB for six regions. The report could carry the same list, and may later, but it would have to be regenerated to change and this list only moves once a year. Ranked by THIS MONTH rather than by rarity, which is the one thing every other section already sorts on.

menu.label: 📘 How each section works
menu.why: app-only: the Markdown report explains each section inline, in the section itself, because a reader scrolling a document is already there. On a phone the sections are separate screens, so the explanations need one place you can reach without opening twenty-four of them. Generated from section-docs.json, so it cannot say anything the per-section info button does not.

reportSectionsAppOmits.## 🗺️ * unseen — closest first: BACKLOG (review item 3): overlaps "Closest spots with unseen birds" and "All unseen reports"; merging the four unseen views is a product decision
reportSectionsAppOmits.## 🔬 iNaturalist unseen: BACKLOG: beta section reading a non-eBird source (iNaturalist), which the app has no client for
reportSectionsAppOmits.## 📅 Year-to-date ABA rarities: BACKLOG: rarity-tracker-only archive of the whole year; the app shows the live ABA alert instead
reportSectionsAppOmits.## 🧭 Trip planner: switched off behind a feature flag (enabled: false) pending a redesign - the code, the panel and the loader are all intact, so this is a hidden section rather than a removed one, and the report still emits it

_menuOmittedAtsWhy: Sections switched off in the app behind `enabled: false` in MENU. They are NOT in `menu` (the app does not list them) but the REPORT still emits them, so section-docs.json still describes them and must not be pruned to match the app. Turning one back on is one word in index.html plus removing it here.
